heuristics.statement: Over fresh masked rho and independent masked trail starts, the fixed Orchard r56 map x -> H(x,rho) has sufficiently random-looking birthday and distinguished-point behavior for the finite search to succeed with probability at least 0.39.
heuristics.scope: The exact selected 56-round Orchard hash, canonical Pallas inputs, one random rho, at most Q+L hash calls and at most 10000 stored trails.
heuristics.extrapolation: The proof gives a >0.4092754 lower bound for an ideal random map. The declared experiments evaluate only a 7-bit closed projection and 20-step full-width trails with an 8-bit output event on 256 organizer seeds; extrapolating to 254-bit collision statistics is heuristic.
heuristics.limitations: No full-width birthday search or concrete full collision has been executed. Small projected maps and short low-byte trail events may conceal algebraic correlations; a about 7 percent reduction in birthday hazard makes the conservative 0.39 bound fail. These experiments cannot establish full-scale probability.

restrictions: The fixed-function success probability relies on score-critical H1; the ideal-map calculation is conditional, and no full 254-bit collision was executed.
The r56 resource score is not asserted to improve the existing review-pending r56 public claims.
